name: Peanut

schedule.notes: Soil must be 65+ F. Plant raw (not roasted) peanuts in their shells, or shelled with skins intact.
After flowering, mound soil up around stems — pods form underground from 'pegs' that drop from flowers.
Lift the whole plant when leaves yellow. Cure for 2 to 3 weeks before shelling.

harvest.cues: Lower leaves yellow, plant looks tired. Dig a test plant; pod kernels should be plump.
harvest.storageNotes: Cure plants whole on a screen 2 to 3 weeks. Shell or store in shells in a cool, dry place. Roast just before eating for best flavor.

varieties.name: Tennessee Red Valencia
varieties.notes: Sweet, 3 to 4 nuts per pod, red skins. Faster-maturing — best for cooler climates.

varieties.name: Virginia Jumbo
varieties.notes: Large nuts, 2 per pod. The ballpark peanut.

notes: Surprises northern gardeners — works as far north as zone 6 with a long warm summer. Loose, sandy soil is non-negotiable; pegs can't push through clay. Roast at 350 F for 15 to 20 minutes when ready to eat.
